confirmedFacts.fact: 3/3 negotiated ACP v1, reported OpenCode 1.18.8, reached the local provider exactly once, returned the expected marker, and ended with end_turn.

confirmedFacts.sample: 1 enabled, 1 external-flags-disabled, and 3 clean HOME runs
confirmedFacts.fact: An OpenCode-native skill under the isolated HOME reached the provider prompt both with and without external-skill disable flags. It was absent in all three clean-HOME runs.
Both RPCs returned successfully in every run. Provider request counts were 2, 1, and 1; the second marker was retained in all runs, while the first marker was absent in the two coalesced runs.
Cancellation after the provider request arrived returned stopReason cancelled and did not issue a second provider request.
2/2 sessions loaded in a new OpenCode process and completed an exact new prompt after the prior process stopped.

confirmedFacts.sample: 1 SIGINT, 1 SIGTERM, and 1 SIGKILL project MCP run
confirmedFacts.fact: OpenCode started the synthetic project MCP twice in every run. Killing only OpenCode terminated the MCP sentinel but left one sentinel child alive after each signal.
Killing the dedicated OpenCode process group terminated the observed MCP sentinel and its inherited child.
OPENCODE_DISABLE_PROJECT_CONFIG=1 prevented every synthetic project MCP start.
A workspace symlink read an external file, a workspace hardlink mutated the external inode, case-only paths aliased, and NFC/NFD Unicode filenames aliased on the tested volume.
Exactly one fixed-port process remained alive, while both --port 0 processes remained alive after two seconds.
Only 5/10 cold concurrent session-list processes succeeded. Two failed with database-locked errors and three with schema-bootstrap races.
The warm-up succeeded and 10/10 warmed concurrent session-list processes succeeded.
Warm operation succeeded, storage pressure left about 6.49 MiB available and produced a typed no-space failure, releasing the filler restored about 266.56 MiB, and the next operation succeeded.

confirmedFacts.sample: 1 synthetic sentinel with inherited and detached descendants
confirmedFacts.fact: The inherited child died with the dedicated process group, while a descendant that created a new session and process group survived. Cleanup by the pre-captured descendant ledger then terminated the escaped process.

confirmedFacts.sample: 1 loopback provider and 1 external TCP reachability discriminator
confirmedFacts.fact: A sandbox-exec profile allowed the exact loopback provider and blocked the external endpoint until the 25-second ACP supervisor timeout. macOS marks sandbox-exec deprecated, so this is mechanism evidence rather than a production adapter decision.

confirmedFacts.sample: 1 signed App Sandbox helper without network.client and 1 with network.client
confirmedFacts.fact: The signed OpenCode helper without network.client negotiated ACP but could not create a session. With network.client it completed the loopback provider prompt and reached the external discriminator, returning the same protocol-response-failure digest as the unsandboxed control.

5/5 pairs loaded the existing session and completed a new prompt: arm64 1.18.5 to 1.18.8, arm64 1.18.8 to 1.18.5, Rosetta x64 1.18.5 to 1.18.8, arm64 to Rosetta x64 at 1.18.8, and Rosetta x64 to arm64 at 1.18.8.

confirmedFacts.sample: 7 synthetic backup, corruption, WAL-loss, and crash scenarios
confirmedFacts.fact: Raw DB/WAL/SHM family restore and checkpointed logical restore both passed integrity, session load, and a new prompt. Removing or corrupting WAL left the base DB integrity check at ok but made the recent session unloadable; corrupting SHM recovered, DB-header corruption recovered from WAL, and full DB replacement was detected.

confirmedFacts.sample: 1 SIGKILL after the provider accepted a request and before the response
confirmedFacts.fact: The session loaded after restart, load issued no provider request, and an explicit follow-up prompt succeeded. OpenCode did not automatically replay the acceptance-uncertain request.

confirmedFacts.sample: 1 forced detach and reattach of a disposable APFS sparse image during an accepted prompt
confirmedFacts.fact: Forced detach succeeded and the in-flight RPC timed out. After reattach, SQLite integrity was ok, the same session loaded without a provider request, and an explicit follow-up prompt ended successfully. This was device removal, not physical power loss.

architectureInvariants: Use a clean allowlisted HOME for every runtime; external-skill flags do not suppress OpenCode-native global skills.
Serialize prompts per OpenCode session and do not equate successful ACP RPCs with independent provider dispatches.
Bind cancellation and reconciliation to provider acceptance rather than ACP send.
Treat OpenCode PID termination as insufficient process custody on macOS.
Launch each runtime in a dedicated process group and independently observe descendants; the positive inherited-child result does not prove containment against process-group escape.
Disable project configuration unless an allowlisted project projection is explicitly required.
Reject or safely materialize symlinks and hardlinks before launch.
Canonicalize and collision-check case and Unicode aliases using target-volume behavior.
Use ACP --port 0 or a separately qualified atomic port lease.
Fence and serialize cold OpenCode state bootstrap.
Classify APFS storage pressure independently from provider failure and revalidate state after capacity returns.
Continuously track descendants independently of process groups; a child can escape by creating a new session and process group.
Do not use sandbox-exec as the production boundary and do not treat App Sandbox network.client as an endpoint allowlist.
Keep exact per-operation egress authorization behind a separately qualified network-enforcement adapter or a contained worker boundary.
Verify the upstream OpenCode asset digest before signing, then attest both the upstream and signed-helper digests.
Back up SQLite with a checkpointed logical snapshot or an atomic DB/WAL/SHM family snapshot; a base-DB integrity check does not prove recent WAL-backed state is present.
Reconcile acceptance-uncertain commands by durable command identity and never infer replay safety from a successful session load.
Treat the five passing version and Rosetta pairs as a bounded compatibility set, not a universal binary policy.
After abrupt storage-device loss, revalidate the complete state family and reconcile the accepted command before marking the runtime reusable.

remainingGates: production macOS endpoint-specific network enforcement and independent qualification
real-provider and OAuth parity in a disposable isolated profile
production continuous descendant custody after adversarial process-group and session escape
physical power-loss and production backup/restore qualification beyond the passing process-crash, forced-device-loss, and corruption matrix
supported macOS-version policy and physical Intel qualification if Intel is supported
